site.name: booking
site.summary: booking-clone Clone of the Booking.com hotel booking funnel (home → city list → area filters → detail → room → booking → confirmation), plus other business-line and supporting pages. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Home: search bar (destination / check-in & out dates / guests), recommended destinations, recent searches, Genius membership prompt, business-line entries in the footer | | `tokyo.html` | Tokyo hotel list: left filter panel (price, stars, rating, amenities, area), right-hand hotel cards (price, rating, review count, distance, free-cancellation tag), sort bar, map entry | | `shinjuku.html` | Shinjuku-area hotel list, same structure as above, pre-filtered to Shinjuku |

run_plan.goal: Execute an exhaustive UX exploration of the Booking.com clone, focusing on the end-to-end hotel booking funnel (Search → List → Detail → Room → Checkout → Confirmation) while validating adjacent business lines and mobile responsiveness.
run_plan.summary: The run will proceed through a primary 'Happy Path' booking flow for the Park Hyatt Tokyo to validate the core checkout logic. It will then branch into secondary flows including filtering on list pages, exploring alternative business lines (Flights/Car Rentals), and verifying account management pages. Finally, it will repeat critical path checks on a mobile viewport to address the high volume of small tap targets identified in the prescan.
assumptions: The site is a static HTML prototype; form submissions will likely redirect to hardcoded next steps rather than processing real data.
The 'Tokyo' and 'Shinjuku' listing pages contain functional filter controls despite being static.
Navigation between business lines (Stays, Flights, etc.) is consistent across all pages.
risk_hotspots: reservation.html: Complex form with multiple input types and validation states.
tokyo.html/shinjuku.html: Filter sidebar density and interaction on mobile viewports.
Global Navigation: High density of small tap targets (<44px) flagged in prescan.
room-selection.html: Price breakdown clarity and 'Continue' button visibility.

phases.title: Primary Booking Funnel (Happy Path)
phases.objective: Validate the core user journey from home page search to booking confirmation.
key_checks: Verify search bar inputs (destination, dates, guests) on index.html.
Navigate to Tokyo list page and select 'Park Hyatt Tokyo'.
Validate hotel details, amenities, and review scores on hotel-detail.html.
Select 'Deluxe King Room' and verify price summary on room-selection.html.
Fill out guest details form on reservation.html (test required field validation if possible).
Confirm successful landing on confirmation.html with correct booking reference.
exit_criteria: No broken links or console errors during the flow.
Price consistency maintained from room selection to confirmation.

phases.title: Listing & Filtering Exploration
phases.objective: Test discovery mechanisms, sorting, and filtering capabilities.
key_checks: Apply filters (Price, Star Rating, Free Cancellation) on tokyo.html.
Navigate to Shinjuku specific list via breadcrumb or link.
Sort results by 'Price (lowest first)' and 'Review score'.
Enter 'Shinjuku Granbell Hotel' detail page to compare layout with Park Hyatt.
Test 'Back to results' navigation functionality.
exit_criteria: Filters visually update the list (or simulate update).
Sorting changes order of hotel cards.
Alternative hotel detail page loads correctly.

phases.title: Adjacent Business Lines
phases.objective: Ensure consistency and basic functionality of non-hotel verticals.
key_checks: Navigate to Flights: Check trip type toggles (Round/One-way) and search inputs.
Navigate to Car Rentals: Verify pick-up/drop-off date inputs and location search.
Navigate to Attractions: Browse category cards and detail views.
Navigate to Airport Taxis: Verify transfer search form.
Check global header consistency across these pages.
exit_criteria: All business line landing pages load without error.
Search forms are present and interactable.
Navigation back to Home/Stays works correctly.

phases.title: Account & Support Systems
phases.objective: Validate user account entry points and support resources.
key_checks: Inspect Sign In/Register forms for layout and social login options.
View 'My Trips' to check upcoming/completed/cancelled tab switching.
Browse Help Center topics and FAQ accordions.
Check Deals page for Genius loyalty program visibility.
Verify footer links (Privacy, Terms) are accessible.
exit_criteria: My Trips tabs switch content visibly.
Help center search and topics are accessible.

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness & Accessibility Audit
phases.objective: Re-test critical paths on mobile viewport to address prescan warnings.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport (e.g., iPhone SE/Pixel 5).
Re-run Phase 1 search flow: Check for overlapping elements or hidden inputs.
Test filter sidebar on tokyo.html: Ensure it opens/closes correctly and is usable.
Verify tap targets on reservation.html: Are inputs large enough? Is the keyboard triggering correctly?
Check hamburger menu or mobile nav behavior if present.
exit_criteria: Core booking flow is completable on mobile.
Document any UI breakage or unusable controls due to screen size.
Verify if small tap target warnings persist in visual inspection.

coverage_targets.features: Exercise search, filtering, sorting, form submission, and tab switching.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat Phase 1 and Phase 2 key interactions on mobile viewport.

notes: Prescan indicates many 'small_tap_target' warnings; prioritize visual verification of these on mobile.
Since this is a static clone, do not expect actual API responses; focus on UI state transitions and layout integrity.
Pay attention to the 'Genius' discount prompts as they appear in multiple contexts (Home, Deals, Header).

Each room is spacious and elegantly designed with floor-to-ceiling windows, deep soaking tubs, and original artwork. The hotel is located in the Nishi-Shinjuku business district, a 12-minute walk from Shinjuku Station. Guests can enjoy the Girandole restaurant for all-day dining, the Peak Bar for cocktails with a view, and the Kozue restaurant for authentic Japanese cuisine. The spa offers a range of treatments in a serene setting on the 45th floor. observation.visible_text: Booking.com Stays Flights Car rentals Attractions Airport taxis JPY List your property Sign in Home > Japan > Tokyo > Shinjuku > Shinjuku Granbell Hotel ★★★ Shinjuku Granbell Hotel 📍 2-14-5 Kabukicho, Shinjuku, Tokyo, 160-0021, Japan · Very Good location — rated 8.4/10 🏙 🛌 🍵 🏊 🌄 About Shinjuku Granbell Hotel Located in the heart of Shinjuku, the Granbell Hotel offers modern accommodations just a 5-minute walk from Shinjuku-Sanchome Station. The hotel features stylish rooms with contemporary Japanese design, a rooftop bar with panoramic city views, and easy access to Tokyo's vibrant nightlife and shopping districts. Each room is thoughtfully designed with comfortable bedding, free WiFi, and modern amenities. The hotel is surrounded by restaurants, convenience stores, and is within walking distance of Kabukicho entertainment district and Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden. Guests can enjoy the on-site restaurant serving Japanese and international cuisine, relax at the rooftop terrace, and explore the many attractions nearby including Meiji Shrine and Takeshita Street in Harajuku. observation.title: Park Hyatt Tokyo - Guest Reviews - Booking.com
observation.visible_text: Booking.com Stays Flights Car rentals Attractions JPY Sign in Home > Tokyo > Park Hyatt Tokyo > Guest reviews Guest reviews Park Hyatt Tokyo 9.4 Exceptional 3,847 reviews Staff 9.6 Facilities 9.4 Cleanliness 9.6 Comfort 9.5 Value for money 8.8 Location 9.6 Free WiFi 9.2 Breakfast 9.3 All reviews (3,847) Most relevant Most recent Highest score Lowest score All Couples (1,234) Families (876) Solo travellers (543) Business (1,194) TK Takeshi Japan · Couple · Deluxe King Room · 3 nights 10 Absolutely perfect in every way 👍 Liked The views from the 47th floor were breathtaking. Staff remembered our names from the first interaction. The New York Grill breakfast is worth every yen. Pool area is serene and never crowded. 👎 Disliked Nothing to complain about. Perhaps the walk from Shinjuku station is a bit long in summer heat, but the hotel shuttle solves that. Reviewed: June 2025 SM Sarah M. United States · Solo traveller · Park King Room · 5 nights 9.6 Lost in Translation vibes, but better 👍 Liked The atmosphere is exactly what you'd hope for. The library lounge is perfect for quiet afternoons. Girandole breakfast buffet has incredible variety. The bed is the most comfortable I've ever slept in. 👎 Disliked Price is steep, but you get what you pay for. The gym can get busy in the early morning. Reviewed: May 2025 LW Li Wei China · Family · Deluxe Twin Room · 4 nights 9.2 Excellent for families with older children 👍 Liked Spacious rooms, impeccable service. The concierge helped us plan our entire Tokyo itinerary. Kids loved the pool. Location is quiet but still accessible to everything. 👎 Disliked Not many kid-specific amenities. The restaurant dress code made dinner with teenagers a bit formal. Would appreciate a kids' menu. Reviewed: April 2025 JB James B. United Kingdom · Business · Park Suite · 2 nights 9.8 The gold standard for business travel 👍 Liked The suite is extraordinary — separate living area, stunning views, and the bathroom alone is larger than most Tokyo hotel rooms. Club lounge access made early mornings productive. Flawless check-in process. 👎 Disliked Honestly nothing. If I had to nitpick, the in-room coffee machine could be upgraded to a proper espresso machine at this price point. Reviewed: March 2025 YK Yuki K. Japan · Couple · Deluxe King Room · 1 night 8.8 Anniversary celebration done right 👍 Liked They arranged a beautiful cake and champagne for our anniversary without us asking — the concierge noticed it in our booking notes. The Peak Bar at sunset is magical. 👎 Disliked For a one-night stay, the value proposition is harder to justify. The minibar prices are quite high even by luxury hotel standards. observation.title: Park Hyatt Tokyo - Booking.com
observation.visible_text: Booking.com Stays Flights Car rentals Attractions Airport taxis JPY List your property Sign in Home > Japan > Tokyo > Shinjuku > Park Hyatt Tokyo ← Back to results ★★★★★ Park Hyatt Tokyo 📍 3-7-1-2 Nishi Shinjuku, Shinjuku, Tokyo, 163-1055, Japan · Excellent location — rated 9.6/10 🏯 🛌 🍵 🏊 🌄 About Park Hyatt Tokyo Occupying the top 14 floors of the 52-story Shinjuku Park Tower, Park Hyatt Tokyo offers panoramic views of the city skyline and Mount Fuji. The hotel features the renowned New York Grill restaurant, a 20-meter indoor swimming pool, and the Club on the Park fitness center with a stunning view of the city. Each room is spacious and elegantly designed with floor-to-ceiling windows, deep soaking tubs, and original artwork. The hotel is located in the Nishi-Shinjuku business district, a 12-minute walk from Shinjuku Station. Guests can enjoy the Girandole restaurant for all-day dining, the Peak Bar for cocktails with a view, and the Kozue restaurant for authentic Japanese cuisine.
